component.name: Omni Launcher
component.summary: One window for every game on this machine

description.p: Omni Launcher finds the games that are already installed on this machine, whatever packaging they came in, and shows them as one cover wall.

It reads Steam libraries, flatpak apps, AppImages, Heroic, Lutris, Faugus, the new Epic Games Launcher and plain desktop entries; it launches them through their own launcher, so a game that is also a Steam shortcut goes through Steam. Cover art comes from Steam's own cache or from SteamGridDB with your own API key, and the source sidebar folds down to an icon rail when you would rather give the covers the space.

Playtime, last played, hidden games, renames and per-game launch options are stored under your XDG directories; nothing is uploaded anywhere. The games you played last wait on a shelf above the wall, and plugins can answer more about a game: the HowLongToBeat lookup that ships with the launcher is one.

A bug-fix release for the wall, the shelf and the playing state. A tile's hover lift stays inside its own box, so the selected cover's ring is no longer cut flat at a scrolled shelf or wall edge; when the detail panel narrows the wall (or the shelf), the game you selected is scrolled back fully into view. The recently played shelf shows a scrollbar whenever it holds more games than fit. A game Steam is asked to start now stays PLAYING until Steam reports the game over instead of a second after the hand-off exits, and Stop signals the game's own processes.

A bug-fix release. Picked SteamGridDB artwork is kept with the launcher's data instead of the cache, is no longer pruned at startup, and is downloaded again when its file goes missing, so a pick survives updates and cache cleanups. The recently played strip leaves room for the hover lift, so the selected cover's ring is no longer clipped.

A feature and bug-check release. Games show a live playing state with Stop and quick-exit diagnostics; per-game launch options add a wrapper, arguments, environment and working folder; Steam collections and Lutris categories become tags with status filters; search ranks acronyms, tags and paths and gains a command palette; Steam update and missing-install state is shown; plugins can offer actions and launch hooks under per-capability grants; and the window can hide while a game runs and returns when it exits, with tray support and focus rescans. The audit pass fixes plugin grant loss, concurrent plugin runs and stdin hangs, Steam update flags and fake download rows, Lutris categories from pga.db, launch-option data loss, wrapper preflight, stop and rescan timers, and hand-off launcher exits.

A bug-fix and responsiveness release. Source discovery now runs concurrently; Steam non-Steam shortcuts match real quoted shortcut paths, no longer hijack a second game with the same name, and keep Steam Input and playtime; Flatpak builds discover their games and launch with the configured working directory again. Cover art and API calls are bounded in time and size, cached images are written atomically, an offline first run no longer suppresses Steam covers for a month, and SteamGridDB misses are remembered instead of re-queried. Plugins are killed on the host when the launcher runs in a sandbox, interrupted installs are not loaded, and archive and HowLongToBeat inputs are bounded. The wall's keyboard and gamepad walk reaches tiles beyond the viewport, transient errors stop resurfacing, and sorting, filtering, scans and config writes do less repeated work.

A stability and polish release. Discovery is asynchronous and finds Flatpak Steam, Prism Launcher and Bottles libraries; plugin installs are checksum-verified, HTTPS-only and confirmed before they run; config, playtime and caches are written atomically with a schema version; the wall is keyboard and gamepad navigable, with favorites, sorting, bulk hide and a persisted window size; and the release workflow now gates the flatpak build on analysis and tests.
AppStream metadata: the homepage, screenshots and a brand colour, so the launcher is presented properly by software centres and by Flathub.

Plugins: a folder with a plugin.json in it and a program the launcher runs, JSON in and JSON out, in any language. Settings holds a plugin store that reads a catalogue from the launcher's own repository, installs a plugin into your plugin folder and removes it again, and each installed plugin gets its section in the detail panel — HowLongToBeat, which ships with the launcher, answers with the main story, main + extra and completionist times.

A recently played shelf above the cover wall: the last ten games started, newest first, with the time played and when. The detail panel keeps Launch and the game's facts, and moves Open folder, Copy, Find art, Rename, Hide and Remove into a cog in its header.

Posters are portrait in every window: the window-shape detection that switched the wall to square grids is gone, and the detail panel preview uses the poster's own shape. The source sidebar folds down to an icon rail.
First packaged release: eight discovery sources, cover art from Steam and SteamGridDB, appearance modes with a GNOME accent palette, playtime, renames and a sandbox-aware host layer.
